title.narrative: Integrated Emergency Education and Lifesaving Shelter Assistance for Vulnerable Populations in Barka, Farwamo, Singaler and Wirkoy Villages in Jamaame District, Jubaland State.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe Community Engagement (CE) sessions conducted under the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Flagship project across Barka, Farwamo, Singaler and Wirkoy, in Jamame district, together with a rapid education assessment undertaken by SADO in January 2026, identified the collapse of education services and acute shelter needs as top community priorities. Communities consistently reported that education services have been largely non-functional since early 2024 due to flooding, repeated climate shocks and the termination of previous support. Barka and Farwamo currently have no functional schools, while Singaler and Wirkoy have flood-damaged but recoverable infrastructure. As a result, hundreds of vulnerable school-aged children remain out of school, facing heightened risks of child labour, early marriage and permanent dropout. In response, the project will address critical, community-identified needs in the four villages through an integrated Education in Emergencies (EiE) and emergency shelter. ltbrgtThe EiE component will restore access to safe, inclusive, and protective learning environments for 700 crisis-affected school-aged children (250 girls, 450 boys) by constructing 8 temporary learning spaces (TLS) in Barka (4) and Farwamo (4) and rehabilitating 8 flood-damaged classrooms in Singaler(4) and Wirkoy (4). 8 latrines will be constructed in Farwamo and Barka, and 8 latrines rehabilitated in Wirkoy and Singalyer. All latrines will be gender segregated. Water tanks will also be rehabilitated for water storage in Farwamo and Baarka. The project will distribute essential individual learning materials to 700 crisis-affected learners to enable immediate participation in formal education. Distribution will be coordinated with school reopening. Teaching materials and school furniture will also be provided to all 4 schools. Training will be provided to 20 teachers on EiE, inclusive and gender-responsive pedagogy, curriculum delivery, learner assessment and basic psychosocial support. Training will be facilitated by qualified trainers in coordination with the MoE and will strengthen teaching quality, learner protection and education continuity in crisis-affected settings. All the 16 teachers and 4 headteachers across the four supported schools will be supported with incentives for the duration of the project to ensure continuity of education services. Incentives will support teacher retention, regular attendance and sustained school operation where no alternative salary mechanisms exist. A five-member committee will be established per school and provided with on-site orientation sessions on oversight, governance and resource mobilisation to strengthen community ownership, accountability, and sustainability. To improve learner retention and enrolment, the project will provide safe, treated drinking water for 700 pupils and 20 teachers, at a rate of 3 litres per person per day, for a duration of 160 days ( 8 Months). Additionally, 250 adolescent girls will receive dignity kits for five months, supporting menstrual hygiene management, school attendance girls’ dignity in line with cluster protection and gender priorities. The project will establish school-level safeguarding mechanisms in all supported schools, including Codes of Conduct, safe and confidential complaint and feedback mechanisms, and referral pathways linked to existing child protection and GBV services. Teachers and committee members will be oriented on child safeguarding and PSEA to ensure learning environments are safe and protective.ltbrgtThe shelter component aims to improve living conditions and dignity for vulnerable households affected by floods and climate shocks. This will be achieved by providing 90 emergency shelter kits (ESK) to vulnerable households particulary the displaced and protection-risk families. SADO will work closely with the shelter cluster and partners like NRC and IOM for an effective shelter project. Over 4740 people will benefit from the interventions. lt/pgt
